text: Hype/promotional language is a studied problem independent of LLMs: biomedical NLP work formalizes automatic detection of promotional phrasing that overstates research significance. (low confidence)

Research on word overuse finds focal words (delve, tapestry, testament, pivotal, underscore, showcasing, crucial, paramount, unwavering) spiked in scientific English and are overused by ChatGPT; human-feedback learning is implicated because participants prefer text containing such words. (medium confidence)

Style-based AI detection is unreliable: OpenAI's retired classifier caught 26% of AI text and falsely flagged 9% of human text; a Stanford study found non-native writing is misclassified. Promotional phrasing alone should not be treated as proof. (medium confidence)

Promotional-tone watchwords in the same guide: 'boasts a', 'vibrant', 'rich', 'profound', 'nestled', 'in the heart of', 'groundbreaking', 'renowned', 'diverse array'; output reads like a travel guide or advertisement rather than neutral encyclopedic prose. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-23)

Wikipedia's AI-writing guide lists significance-inflation markers: 'stands/serves as', 'is a testament', 'crucial/pivotal role', 'underscores its importance', 'reflects broader', 'setting the stage for'; LLMs attach broader symbolic meaning to arbitrary facts, e.g. a name change 'highlighting the enduring legacy'. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-23)
The Wikipedia guide says GPT-4-era models were more blatantly positive than newer ones, which use subtler positivity, so lexical lists date quickly. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-23)
